task_type: production data-parity diagnosis and root repair
requested_outcome: The vacation and event availability sliders use one deterministic supplier-authoritative contract, match the intended legacy tab semantics, and remain correct across dates, reloads and future code changes.
natural_destination: The public VII homepage vacation and event availability sliders and their dedicated landing pages
authorization_boundary: Read the legacy site and supplier-backed public APIs, change VII source and tests, and verify locally; do not mutate supplier data, CMS, database, secrets, DNS or publish without separate authorization.

lesson_bundle.reason: The task is VII-specific and depends on canonical project behavior.
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: Treat the API as availability truth and the legacy site as a semantic reference, not as an unverified source of current inventory.

lesson_bundle.reason: The defect is a data identity, filtering and ordering mismatch.
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: Prove every displayed card maps to a public catalog entity and a complete verified supplier offer.

lesson_bundle.reason: The same data must remain consistent across API, slider, landing and reload.
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: Use one shared deterministic ordering and deduplication contract across the affected family.

lesson_bundle.reason: The user explicitly reports recurring regressions.
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: Add automated contract tests for all vacation tabs, all event tabs, duplicates, missing entities, stale dates and repeatability.

lesson_bundle.reason: Both desktop and mobile public sliders are affected.
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: Verify loading, success, empty, error, tab switch and reload on desktop and mobile.

lesson_bundle.reason: A later release must preserve exact candidate identity and evidence.
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: Do not claim public completion from local code or tests.

predicted_rejections.rejection: The first visible cards still change between reloads even though the API response is stable.
predicted_rejections.prevention: Remove document-seeded client reshuffling from verified availability rails and use a shared stable comparator.
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: Two renders of identical API data produce identical identities, order, prices and dates.

predicted_rejections.rejection: A legacy venue is missing or a new venue appears without a clear reason.
predicted_rejections.prevention: Classify each delta as supplier availability, public publication, identity join, completeness or stale legacy evidence.
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: The audit reports an explicit reason for every legacy/API/display delta.

predicted_rejections.rejection: Events show a venue with the wrong offer when the supplier returns more than one offer for the same venue.
predicted_rejections.prevention: Select one canonical complete offer per venue before joining to the public catalog.
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: Duplicate-offer fixtures always choose the same best complete offer.

predicted_rejections.rejection: The fix works for one tab but fails for Thursday, Friday or weekend boundaries.
predicted_rejections.prevention: Bind every tab to a named date-window contract using the Israel timezone.
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: All five vacation periods and all three event presets pass date-boundary tests.

affected_family: vacation home slider and dedicated last-minute landing
desktop and mobile reload and tab-switch states

midpoint_gate.trigger: After the root mechanism is proven and shared selection functions pass focused tests, before broad build or any release action
checks: All vacation and event tab date windows are deterministic
Verified offer order is stable across repeated renders
Identity, completeness and deduplication fixtures pass
Every observed legacy/API delta has a classified cause

attack_questions: Can a document seed or reload still reorder verified offers?
Can two offers for one venue produce a mismatched card or price?
Can a stale, incomplete or unpublished entity leak into a slider?
Do Israel timezone boundaries change a tab date unexpectedly?
Does the same API payload produce different desktop and mobile cards?
adversarial_close.natural_destination_evidence: Rendered local production build at desktop and mobile plus direct API response comparison for every tab
adversarial_close.affected_family_evidence: Focused contract tests, production build and a machine-readable parity audit

effectiveness.baseline: Legacy and new sliders differ in membership and order, and verified offer rails are reshuffled in the browser using a document seed.
effectiveness.target: Every tab has deterministic dates, one canonical complete offer per public entity, stable API-to-render order and zero unexplained parity deltas.
